hints.content:
$f'(x)>0$ means $f$ is **increasing**.

$f'(x)<0$ means $f$ is **decreasing**.

$f''(x)>0$ means the slope of $f$ is increasing ($f$ is **concave up**).

$f''(x)<0$ means the slope of $f$ is decreasing ($f$ is **concave down**).

| | $f'(x)>0$ | $f'(x)<0$
:- | :- | :-: | :-:
| | $f$ is **increasing** | $f$ is **decreasing**
$f''(x)>0$ | $f$ is **concave up** |  ![A curve moves upward with increasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/fad1dc95cd761b6e7f4c581c7093841fcf16029a) | ![A curve moves downward with decreasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/88e8d1ff71cbe909ea256814c06e1ff2df39bd5e)
$f''(x)<0$ | $f$ is **concave down** | ![A curve moves upward with decreasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/f9425dbee4d4f73f6188a62f88f637018843d7c8) | ![A curve moves downward with increasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/4d64d76d6423a90abf605dfe2b856e7327f92a0c)

We are asked to find an interval where $f'(x)<0$ and $f''(x)>0$, so we need an interval where the graph of $f$ has this general shape:

 ![A curve moves downward with decreasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/88e8d1ff71cbe909ea256814c06e1ff2df39bd5e)

Visually, this is where $f'(x)<0$ and $f''(x)>0$.

![The graph of function f has 2 portions of the curve highlighted. Each portion moves downward concave up, from about (negative 1, 1.5) to (0, 0), and from (3, 0) to about (4.5, negative 9).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/3fad372d83f486c3ffa8335720d79591b8d95ee0)

Now we can check each option:

Interval | Shape | Is $f'(x)<0$ and $f''(x)>0$?
:-: | :-: | :-:
$-4<x<-3$ | ![A curve moves upward with increasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/842593fcfd6a52a51cd66950f88ff7cd344d7af3) | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $f''(x)>0$ but $f'(x)>0$.
$-3<x<-2$ | ![A curve moves upward with decreasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/422cf5924dbecfc98054d87696663b0145ce07e6) | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $f'(x)>0$ and $f''(x)<0$.
$0<x<1$ | ![A curve moves upward with increasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/842593fcfd6a52a51cd66950f88ff7cd344d7af3) | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $f''(x)>0$ but $f'(x)>0$.

The curve starts in quadrant 3, moves downward concave up to about (negative 4.5, negative 9), moves upward concave up to about (negative 3.5, negative 3), continues upward concave down through (negative 3, 0) to about (negative 2, 3.5), moves downward concave down to about (negative 1, 1.5), continues downward concave up to about (0, 0), moves upward concave up to about (1, 1.5), continues upward concave down to about (2, 3.5), moves downward concave down through (3, 0) to about (3.5, negative 3), continues downward concave up to about (4.5, negative 9), moves upward concave up, and ends in quadrant 4.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/2ffe05d5ecea7365ab18ac30ec98defe983ad7b8)

**Select all the intervals where $f'(x)<0$ and $f''(x)>0$.**
